_comment: Hand-written additions per registry id, merged by gen_reference.py. Keys: 'note' (HTML, appended to the description), 'perm' (name of the Project Settings permission the row needs, see EngineApi.cpp perm::allowed), 'script_sig' / 'script_returns' (the Lua/Python call when it differs from the registry signature), 'examples' ({lua, python} source, rendered with the language switcher). Steps 3-8 of Thema 79 fill this per group.

log.note: Lua also accepts a number; Python only a str.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

-- True when target lies within coneDeg degrees around the direction
-- (fx, fy, fz) this entity faces.
function M.canSee(self, target, fx, fy, fz, coneDeg)
    local x, y, z = horizon.getPosition(self.entityId)
    local tx, ty, tz = horizon.getPosition(target)
    local dx, dy, dz = horizon.math.normalize3(tx - x, ty - y, tz - z)
    local limit = horizon.math.cos(horizon.math.radians(coneDeg / 2))
    return horizon.math.dot3(dx, dy, dz, fx, fy, fz) >= limit
end

return M
examples.python:
import horizon

class ViewCone(horizon.Behavior):
    def can_see(self, target, fx, fy, fz, cone_deg):
        """True when target lies within cone_deg degrees around (fx, fy, fz)."""
        x, y, z = horizon.getPosition(self.entity_id)
        tx, ty, tz = horizon.getPosition(target)
        dx, dy, dz = horizon.math.normalize3(tx - x, ty - y, tz - z)
        limit = horizon.math.cos(horizon.math.radians(cone_deg / 2))
        return horizon.math.dot3(dx, dy, dz, fx, fy, fz) >= limit

string.find.note: In Lua, add 1 before handing the result to string.sub.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

-- "volume = 75" -> "volume", 75. Positions count from 0.
local function parse(line)
    local eq = horizon.string.find(line, "=")
    if eq < 0 then return nil end
    local key = horizon.string.trim(horizon.string.substring(line, 0, eq))
    local rest = horizon.string.substring(line, eq + 1, horizon.string.length(line))
    return key, horizon.string.toNumber(rest)
end

function M.onStart(self)
    local key, value = parse("volume = 75")
    if key then horizon.log(key .. " is " .. value) end
end

return M

local M = {}

function M.onStart(self)
    -- Without this, every launch rolls the same numbers. Seed in one
    -- script only: every seed restarts the sequence for all of them.
    horizon.random.seed(os.time())
end

function M.roll(self)
    local eyes = horizon.random.rangeInt(1, 6)      -- 1 to 6, both included
    local critical = horizon.random.chance(0.05)     -- one in twenty
    return eyes, critical
end

return M
examples.python:
import time
import horizon

class Dice(horizon.Behavior):
    def on_start(self):
        # Without this, every launch rolls the same numbers. Seed in one
        # script only: every seed restarts the sequence for all of them.
        horizon.random.seed(int(time.time()))

    def roll(self):
        eyes = horizon.random.rangeInt(1, 6)     # 1 to 6, both included
        critical = horizon.random.chance(0.05)   # one in twenty
        return eyes, critical

time.pause.note: Input actions stop arriving unless they have Fires while the game is paused ticked.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

-- "Pause" is an input action with "Fires while the game is paused"
-- ticked; without it the second press would never arrive.
function M.onInputPressed(self, name)
    if name ~= "Pause" then return end
    if horizon.time.isPaused() then
        horizon.time.resume()
    else
        horizon.time.pause()
    end
end

function M.onCollisionEnter(self, other)
    horizon.time.hitStop(0.1)   -- a landed hit freezes for a tenth of a second
end

return M

time.hitStop.note: 0 or less does nothing, and does not end a hit stop that is running.

timer.after.note: 0 also when 64 timers are already running.

timer.every.note: 0 when the interval is under 0.001 seconds or 64 timers are already running.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

function M.onStart(self)
    self.autosave = horizon.timer.every(30)
    self.hint = horizon.timer.after(5)
end

function M.onTimer(self, handle)
    if handle == self.autosave then
        horizon.log("autosave")
    elseif handle == self.hint then
        horizon.log("Press E to open the door")
    end
    -- any other handle belongs to another script
end

return M

timer.cancelAll.note: That includes the timers of every other script and of the GameInstance.

datetime.now.note: Accurate only to about a minute, see the known issue.

examples.lua:
local M = {}

local DAYS = { [0] = "Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday",
               "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday" }

function M.onStart(self)
    local now = horizon.datetime.now()
    horizon.log("Today is " .. DAYS[horizon.datetime.weekday(now)] .. ", "
                .. horizon.datetime.format(now, "%d.%m.%Y"))
    -- To the second: from Lua itself until the precision issue is fixed.
    horizon.log("It is " .. os.date("%H:%M:%S"))
end

return M
examples.python:
import time
import horizon

DAYS = ["Sunday", "Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday",
        "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday"]

class ClockLabel(horizon.Behavior):
    def on_start(self):
        now = horizon.datetime.now()
        day = DAYS[horizon.datetime.weekday(now)]
        horizon.log(f"Today is {day}, {horizon.datetime.format(now, '%d.%m.%Y')}")
        # To the second: from Python itself until the precision issue is fixed.
        horizon.log("It is " + time.strftime("%H:%M:%S"))

datetime.format.note: %M and %S are accurate only to about a minute, see the known issue.

datetime.minute.note: Accurate only to about a minute, see the known issue.

datetime.second.note: Not usable until the known issue is fixed.

local M = {}

function M.onUpdate(self, dt)
    local x, y, z = horizon.getPosition(self.entityId)
    -- Four numbers per position and color, the fourth is ignored.
    -- 0 seconds: drawn this frame only, so the shapes follow the entity.
    horizon.debug.line(x, y, z, 0,   x, y - 2, z, 0,   1, 0, 0, 1,   0)
    horizon.debug.sphere(x, y - 2, z, 0,   0.25,   0, 1, 0, 1,   0)
end

return M
